theme: wildcard: a hedge-fund alternative-data buyer who has seen every vendo
ten_ideas: 1. Camping/outdoor-recreation reservation systems (Recreation.gov RIDB, ReserveCalifornia, GoingToCamp) as a book-ahead / sold-out-inventory-with-cancellations analogue and a competing-travel-dollar signal — HIT (method repos, no bundled historical data).

2. Peer-to-peer car-sharing (Turo) datasets/scrapers as a marketplace-elasticity analogue (dynamic pricing, take rate, host supply economics) — MISS on GitHub (search only surfaces Turo's own marketing pages).

3. Meta 'Data for Good' mobility/movement-range datasets as a regional travel-intensity proxy — PARTIAL HIT (tooling exists to consume the data; no repo bundles the underlying Meta CSVs, which Meta has been sunsetting).

4. Uber Movement travel-time data as an urban mobility / local-activity proxy — MISS (no useful repos surfaced before search budget/rate limits hit; Uber Movement itself was deprecated by Uber in 2023-24, likely explaining GitHub thinness).

5. Company job-board scrapers (Greenhouse/Lever public APIs) pulling Airbnb's own postings by department/geo as a headcount/hiring-intensity proxy — HIT (a generic scraper explicitly demos Airbnb as a target company).

6. SafeGraph-style foot-traffic 'patterns' data (places visited, dwell time) as a destination-demand proxy, plus methods for handling its known censoring/truncation — PARTIAL HIT (a couple of small demo/analysis repos; no bundled current data, SafeGraph patterns product has largely closed off free access).

7. Buy-now-pay-later (Klarna/Affirm/Afterpay) adoption/usage open datasets as an RNPL-adjacent consumer-credit-strain proxy outside STRs — MISS (nothing on GitHub; BNPL usage data is proprietary/panel-only).
8. RV rental (Outdoorsy/RVshare) and boat rental (GetMyBoat) marketplace data as adjacent 'alternative accommodation/experience' supply-and-pricing analogues — MISS (no data or scraper repos found).

9. Wayback Machine / web-archive tooling to reconstruct historical airbnb.com and AirDNA market pages that are otherwise gone (matches CONTEXT gap #17 directly) — HIT (mature, widely used Python client).

10. Cloudflare Radar (internet traffic, bot/crawler share, AI-referral share) API clients and bot-directory data as an AI-referral-traffic and web-engagement proxy (matches CONTEXT gaps #5 and #19) — HIT (SDKs in three languages plus a maintained bot-UA directory).

candidates.name: juftin/camply
candidates.what_it_holds: Python CLI/TUI (651 stars, MIT, actively maintained, 257 commits) that polls Recreation.gov, ReserveCalifornia, Yellowstone Lodges, and GoingToCamp-platform state park systems for campsite cancellations/availability at sold-out campgrounds and pushes notifications (email/Slack/SMS/Telegram/webhook). No bundled historical data; it is a live-polling method.
candidates.why_useful: Outdoor-recreation booking pace is a competing-travel-dollar signal and a clean analogue for the RNPL/cancellation-monitoring thesis (watching for cancellations at capacity-constrained inventory) — same mechanic as the STR cancellation/lead-time question (gap #3), just on a different asset class; also a template for point-in-time capacity-utilization capture.

candidates.name: nirholas/x402-campsites
candidates.what_it_holds: TypeScript service (Apache-2.0, 4 stars, 6 commits, created Sep 2026) wrapping the official RIDB campground-metadata API plus Recreation.gov's public, keyless site-level availability API; exposes both as a pay-per-call (USDC micropayment) HTTP/MCP tool with a fallback fixture catalog of 8 campgrounds when no RIDB key is set.
candidates.why_useful: Confirms Recreation.gov's live-availability endpoint is public and keyless (no scraping/ToS issue) — a ready acquisition path for outdoor-recreation capacity-utilization as a competing-travel-dollar proxy.

candidates.name: mheadd/node-ridb (representative of ~6 RIDB API wrapper repos: AJFunk/ridb-node, boscomonkey/doi-rec-data, jtbradt/ridbAPI, pipeworx-io/mcp-recreation-gov, Dnakitare/recreation-data-manager)
candidates.what_it_holds: Thin client libraries (Node/Ruby/.NET/Java/MCP) for USDA/DOI's Recreation Information Database (RIDB) API — facility, campsite, and permit metadata across all US federal recreation lands. No bundled data, needs a free API key.
candidates.why_useful: Federal outdoor-recreation demand is a free, government-run book-ahead system that scales across the whole US; a maintained client makes it trivial to build a national capacity-utilization index as a demand-substitute/complement signal.
candidates.last_activity: mostly stale (2015-2020), pipeworx-io/mcp-recreation-gov and Dnakitare/recreation-data-manager updated 2026

candidates.name: logiover/greenhouse-job-board-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Unofficial, MIT-licensed Apify actor description (repo itself is a doc/marketing page, 0 stars) that scrapes any company's public Greenhouse job board (job IDs, titles, full descriptions, department/office hierarchy, post dates) with named example targets including Airbnb, Anthropic, Stripe, Datadog. Runs on Apify infra, not the repo code itself; no API key or login needed since Greenhouse job boards are public JSON endpoints.
candidates.why_useful: Airbnb's own Greenhouse board is public; open-role counts/departments/geos over time is a free, non-financial headcount and functional-investment proxy (engineering vs. trust&safety vs. international expansion hiring) that is genuinely non-obvious as an 'Airbnb search' and ties to gap #15 (company-structure signals / headcount proxy).
candidates.time_coverage: point-in-time snapshots only if run repeatedly; no history bundled

candidates.name: firmanaf/MobiVista
candidates.what_it_holds: QGIS Processing plugin (MIT, 3 stars, released Oct 2025) that ingests Meta 'Data for Good' Movement Map CSVs (region IDs, distance-band bins, dates) and produces spatially aggregated layers, visual analytics, and synthetic origin-destination flows. Ships only the plugin code, not Meta's underlying mobility CSVs.
candidates.why_useful: If Meta's Data for Good mobility program still issues movement-range data (access has been narrowing), this is a ready pipeline to turn it into regional travel-intensity indices for the NA/EMEA/LatAm/APAC mix question; worth a follow-up to check current Meta program access status before building on it.
candidates.geography: wherever Meta issues Movement Maps (historically global, now restricted)
candidates.time_coverage: depends on Meta program access, not in repo

candidates.name: mpayson/safegraph-patterns
candidates.what_it_holds: Minimal ArcGIS-JS demo app (0 stars, 1 commit, built for an Esri Partner Conference) for exploring SafeGraph Patterns (POI-level visit-count) data. No data bundled, no license stated; essentially a UI shell.
candidates.why_useful: Confirms SafeGraph Patterns schema/structure is documented in the open even where the underlying paid dataset is not; low standalone value but a pointer for anyone with SafeGraph/Advan/Placer.ai access.

candidates.name: zachporreca/safegraph_DiD_piecewise_likelihood_MLE
candidates.what_it_holds: Julia script (1 star, no license stated) implementing a difference-in-differences / piecewise-likelihood MLE estimator specifically built to handle the censoring and truncation quirks of publicly released SafeGraph Patterns data.
candidates.why_useful: If the team ever gets hold of any POI-visit panel (SafeGraph, Advan, or a municipal foot-traffic dataset) with similar top/bottom-coding, this is a directly reusable estimator rather than a from-scratch build.

candidates.name: akamhy/waybackpy
candidates.what_it_holds: Mature, actively maintained Python library + CLI (604 stars, also packaged on conda-forge) wrapping the Internet Archive Wayback Machine's Availability, CDX, and Save-Page-Now APIs: fetch, list, and trigger archival of any URL's historical snapshots.
candidates.why_useful: Directly matches CONTEXT gap #17's explicit call for 'Wayback Machine tooling (archived airbnb.com pages, archived AirDNA market pages)' — this is the standard, well-supported tool to pull historical renders of pages that are no longer live (old AirDNA city sample pages, old Airbnb help-center/press pages, historical STR-ordinance pages).
candidates.time_coverage: as far back as Internet Archive's crawls go per URL

candidates.name: microlinkhq/cloudflare-bot-directory
candidates.what_it_holds: Committed JSON/data files (18 stars) listing 500+ verified crawler and search-engine bot user-agents as published by Cloudflare Radar's bot directory (includes AI-crawler identifiers like GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot).
candidates.why_useful: Matches CONTEXT gap #19 ('AI-referral traffic: bot/crawler share datasets') directly — a maintained, structured list of bot UAs is the building block for classifying web-log or CDN traffic into AI-agent vs. human vs. search-engine share, relevant to how Airbnb's own site traffic mix may be shifting toward AI-agent referrals/bookings.
candidates.time_coverage: current snapshot, updated periodically as Cloudflare's directory changes
candidates.license: not stated in summary, check repo

candidates.name: bgpkit/radar-rs
candidates.what_it_holds: Unofficial Rust SDK (2 stars) for the Cloudflare Radar API, which exposes global internet-traffic volume, outage detection, protocol-adoption, and (with an API token) bot/AI-crawler traffic-share time series.
candidates.why_useful: A code-level client for the same Cloudflare Radar data referenced in gaps #5 and #19; useful once someone registers a free Cloudflare Radar API token to pull historical internet-traffic and AI-bot-share series as an engagement/AI-disintermediation proxy for travel-booking sites broadly.
candidates.time_coverage: per Cloudflare Radar API history (varies by metric)

candidates.name: RalfKoch/CloudflareRadarKit
candidates.what_it_holds: Zero-dependency Swift client for the Cloudflare Radar API (global internet traffic, outages, protocol adoption), targeting iOS 17+/macOS 14+.
candidates.why_useful: Same Cloudflare Radar data source as bgpkit/radar-rs, in Swift; listed for completeness since it's a different language ecosystem — do not build both, pick one client.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: bgpkit/radar-rs (same underlying Cloudflare Radar API, different language binding)

candidates.name: openskynetwork/opensky-api
candidates.what_it_holds: Official Python/Java bindings (466 stars, actively maintained by OpenSky Network e.V.) for the OpenSky Network REST API: free, real-time and (via their research data portal) historical global ADS-B flight-state vectors (position, altitude, callsign) crowdsourced from a receiver network.
candidates.why_useful: Directly matches CONTEXT gap #10 ('Airline/rail/road capacity and traffic: ... OpenSky/ADS-B'); flight volumes by route/region are a real-time proxy for cross-border and long-haul leisure travel intensity feeding into nights/regional mix, and OpenSky additionally has a historical Impala/Trino research database (not in this repo, but reachable via the same client) for point-in-time flight counts.
candidates.time_coverage: real-time; historical research DB goes back to ~2019
candidates.size_hint: client library only, no bundled data
candidates.license: check repo (OpenSky Network e.V., typically MIT/GPL for bindings)

candidates.name: ashermanwmf/pageviewapi
candidates.what_it_holds: Small client/wrapper for Wikimedia's official Pageviews API, returning per-article, per-day pageview counts back to mid-2015.
candidates.why_useful: Matches CONTEXT gap #5 ('Wikipedia pageviews tooling') directly; Wikipedia pageviews for 'Airbnb', 'short-term rental', competitor articles, or destination-city articles are a free, long-history, point-in-time-clean (pageviews are immutable once logged) engagement/interest proxy that has not been tested by the team yet.
candidates.size_hint: client only, API pull required for data
candidates.last_activity: check repo (appears stale; the canonical/actively-maintained alternative is Wikimedia's own `wikimedia/mediawiki-services-pageview-api` or the `mwviews`/`pageviewapi` PyPI package — flag for a follow-up scout to find the best-maintained client)

notes: Operational: this session's WebSearch tool had already exhausted its 200-query budget before this scout started (shared across whatever else was running concurrently), so all open-web discovery had to route through gh search repos and WebFetch against Bing/GitHub pages instead. WebFetch to github.com's own /search endpoint returned HTTP 429 for about an hour; Bing rendered pages did not reliably surface github.com results even with site:github.com (likely JS-rendered result cards not present in the fetched HTML) - direct WebFetch to specific known/guessed repo URLs worked fine and was the most productive path. gh search repos multi-word queries frequently returned empty arrays even for terms that should match (e.g. 'wikimedia pageviews pageviewapi', 'opensky network ADS-B flight traffic dataset') while the same concepts as single-token queries ('pageviewapi', 'opensky-network', 'waybackpy') returned strong results - GitHub's search API appears to AND every token literally against name+description+topics with no fuzziness, so future scouts should prefer single distinctive tokens (a product/library name) over descriptive phrases, and fall back to 2-3 single-token queries per idea rather than one long natural-language query. True dead ends worth recording so nobody re-runs them: Turo, Outdoorsy/RVshare/GetMyBoat, Klarna/Affirm/Afterpay usage panels, Eventbrite/Ticketmaster bulk event datasets, ski-resort/snowfall-linked travel data, cruise-line advance-booking-curve data, and Hipcamp - none of these have any GitHub presence beyond unrelated clone/demo apps or the vendors' own marketing pages; if any of these matter, the path is a paid vendor (AirDNA-style) or a direct company IR/10-K disclosure (NCLH does disclose 'advance ticket sales' as a balance-sheet line - that's a filings pull, not a GitHub one). Two ideas came back partial/degraded because the underlying vendor program has been shrinking free access: Meta 'Data for Good' Movement Maps (tooling exists, e.g. MobiVista, but Meta has been narrowing who can register for the raw CSVs - worth a scout checking current Meta Data for Good access terms) and SafeGraph Patterns (same pattern - schema/analysis repos exist from ~2020-2024 but the free/academic access window SafeGraph offered has largely closed; Advan Research is the current commercial successor and unlikely to have a GitHub-free analogue). Two ideas resolved as genuinely good hits that a follow-up agent should build on: (1) waybackpy for pulling historical airbnb.com/AirDNA page renders per the CONTEXT gap #17 ask, and (2) the OpenSky Network API/client for real-time and historical (via their Trino research DB, not in this repo but same auth) global flight volumes as a travel-capacity proxy per gap #10 - OpenSky's historical database specifically deserves a dedicated scout since it is not a GitHub-hosted dataset itself but the client here is the door to it. The Greenhouse job-board scraper idea is worth flagging up because the generic tool's own example list names Airbnb specifically, meaning a follow-up agent could point it at Airbnb's real board today (careers.airbnb.com uses Greenhouse) and start a point-in-time open-roles-by-department/geo time series with zero scraping-ToS ambiguity since Greenhouse job boards are public JSON APIs by design, not gated pages - this reads on gap #15 (headcount as an investment-intensity signal) without touching airbnb.com itself, so it does not trip rule #6.
